text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Quebec priest slain in Rwanda: Cleric, 61, insisted on returning to Africa after 1996 surgery in Montreal.
- Villages fight over Voisey's riches: Nickel-mine deal being held up.
- Hostage crisis strategy reached: Japan, Peru agree on talks with rebels.
- Reform planning blizzard of videos: Screen strategy may cost $12-million.
- Life moves smartly at military prison.
- Ontario blowing its horn: Executives to join Premier in print, TV ad campaign touting province for investment.
- The Altamira attraction: Firms are battling for control of the mutual fund manager, despite recent troubles, because it's part of the best growth game in town.
- Cow hormone smuggling foiled: Drug seizures raise fears about milk.
- Experts take a shine to gold but still skeptical on bonds.
- Ottawa won't let foreigners own more of phone firms: But new trade offer calls for quick end to Telesat and Teleglobe monopolies.
- Royal Oak holds out for B.C. money.
- Making a killing, literally, on the VSE.
